facts.statement: Execution cf997605885642759ee33920e2c9e2ef records reach_passed=true with terminal_error_m=0.007642608585867386 m inside the 0.01 m reach tolerance, but holding_position_passed=false, holding_speed_passed=false and joint_reach_holding_passed=false.

Over the retained final holding window (6 rows, sample_times_s=0.30-0.35 s) the world-tip error_m spans 0.007642608585867386-0.05813810428573256 m and speed_m_s spans 0.6351726092425104-1.5810152739742807 m/s, versus settling criteria position_limit_m=0.01 m and speed_limit_m_s=0.02 m over window_s=0.05 s; the recorded tip speed exceeds the speed limit by roughly 79x at its maximum.

The run recorded deadline_misses=35 with stopping_counts User_Requested_Stop=34 and Solve_Succeeded=1, mean_update_s=17.26331904856488 per 0.01 s control period, and per-update update_wall_s of 29.35 s (update 0, F536), 18.46 s (update 5, F505), 18.59 s (update 15, F599); effective_horizon is 10 at updates 0 and 10 but truncated to 5 at update 30.

The configured recipe carries holding_tip_speed_weight=0.0, terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.0, tip_speed_scale_m_s=0.02 and terminal_weight=5.0; the recorded final-window tip speed (up to 1.581 m/s) is far above the 0.02 m/s settling limit, which is consistent with (but not proof of) no active tip-speed penalty at hold; raw weight magnitudes alone do not establish cost-term importance without actual contributions/scaling.
